# Proverbs 27 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Do-not-boast about-tomorrow, for you-do-not-know what a-day will-bring-forth.

**2** Let-a-stranger praise-you and-not your-[own]-mouth, a-foreigner and-not your-[own]-lips.

**3** Heavy [is] a-stone and-weighty [is] sand, but-[the]-provocation-of a-fool [is]-heavier than-both-of-them.

**4** Cruelty [is in]-wrath and-a-flood [is in]-anger, but-who can-stand before jealousy?

**5** Better [is]-rebuke open than-love hidden.

**6** Faithful [are the]-wounds-of a-friend, but-excessive [are the]-kisses-of an-enemy.

**7** A-soul satisfied tramples a-honeycomb, but-to-a-soul hungry every bitter-thing [is] sweet.

**8** Like-a-bird wandering from-its-nest, so [is] a-man wandering from-his-place.

**9** Oil and-incense gladden [the]-heart, and-[the]-sweetness-of a-friend from-counsel-of [the]-soul.

**10** Your-friend and-[the]-friend-of your-father do-not-forsake, and-[the]-house-of your-brother do-not-enter in-[the]-day-of your-calamity. Better [is] a-neighbor near than-a-brother far.

**11** Be-wise, my-son, and-gladden my-heart, and-I-will-return a-word to-one-reproaching-me.

**12** A-prudent-one sees evil [and]-hides-himself; simple-ones pass-on [and]-are-punished.

**13** Take his-garment, for he-has-become-surety [for a]-stranger, and-in-behalf-of a-foreign-woman seize-him-as-pledge.

**14** One-blessing his-friend with-a-voice loud in-the-morning early — a-curse it-will-be-considered for-him.

**15** A-dripping continual on-a-day-of driving-rain and-a-woman-of contentions are-alike.

**16** One-hiding-her hides wind, and-oil [on] his-right-hand encounters.

**17** Iron by-iron is-sharpened, and-a-man sharpens [the]-face-of his-friend.

**18** One-tending a-fig-tree will-eat its-fruit, and-one-guarding his-master will-be-honored.

**19** As-the-water the-face to-the-face, so the-heart-of the-man to-the-man.

**20** Sheol and-Abaddon are-never-satisfied, and-[the]-eyes-of man are-never-satisfied.

**21** A-refining-pot for-silver and-a-furnace for-gold, and-a-man according-to his-praise.

**22** If you-pound the-fool in-a-mortar among-grain with-a-pestle, his-folly will-not-depart from-upon-him.

**23** Know well [the]-face-of your-flock; set your-heart to-[the]-herds,

**24** For not forever [is] wealth, and-does a-crown [endure] to-generation [and]-generation?

**25** Grass departs and-new-growth appears, and-herbs-of [the]-mountains are-gathered,

**26** Lambs [are] for-your-clothing, and-[the]-price-of a-field [are]-goats,

**27** And-enough goats'-milk for-your-food, for-food-of your-household, and-life for-your-maidens.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **27:5-6**: Open rebuke over hidden love; faithful wounds over enemy kisses. The pair emphasizes that genuine relationship involves honesty, even painful honesty.

- **27:17**: Barzel be-varzel yechad — 'iron by iron sharpens.' The most celebrated friendship proverb after 17:17. Mutual sharpening through honest interaction.

- **27:19**: Ka-mayim ha-panim la-panim — 'as water, the face to the face.' The heart mirrors the true self, just as water reflects the face.

— EMET
